title: Voxelgame player guides
description: Task-based Voxelgame guides: getting started, a searchable controls reference, a first survival day and every crafting recipe, each traced to the game source.
headline:
Learn the game,
one task at a time.
lead: Short, task-based guides for what you can do in the game today. Every key, number and recipe is traced to the game's source code, and planned features stay marked as planned.
comingLead: These guides are next, in the order players need them. Each waits on a source check and, where noted, on screenshots from a disposable headless session.

guides.title: Getting started: your first session
guides.headline:
Your first session,
from menu to saved world.
guides.summary: The start menu, creating a world, moving, reading the screen, opening your pack, switching modes, and saving safely.
guides.lead: Everything you need for the first twenty minutes: starting a world, moving around, finding your pack and leaving without losing anything.

verification.method: Every key, number and message below was read from the game source at the audited commit and traced to a ledger entry. The four screenshots come from the same commit's release build, run headless against a throwaway world. The Target info, Speed FOV and Damage bob settings were checked against game commit 6acf338 (main 4bd6541), which came after the audited commit.
verification.limits: This is a source-checked guide, not a recorded play session: nobody drove the game by keyboard for this page. Interface wording and layout can change in later game versions.

blocks.text: Voxelgame is played with a keyboard and mouse only. There is no gamepad support, and keys cannot be rebound. Keys are read by position, so on an AZERTY or other layout use the keys that sit where [[W]] [[A]] [[S]] [[D]] sit on a QWERTY keyboard. {{input-devices-and-layout}}

The window opens at 1280 × 720 and cannot be made smaller than 800 × 450. Press [[F11]] or [[Alt]] + [[Enter]] to toggle borderless fullscreen; the game does not remember fullscreen between launches. {{window-and-fullscreen}}

Installing and updating the game is not covered by this guide yet; it is on the list of guides still to write. On Linux, an active Pinyin input method under X11 can swallow movement keys; that problem is unresolved in the game.

blocks.alt: The Voxelgame start menu showing world, settings and study controls, with a wireframe cube on the left.
blocks.caption: The start menu. Headless capture of the game at the audited commit (1280 × 720, fresh disposable world). The panel is drawn translucent over the scene.

blocks.text: Use Continue to enter the current world or Worlds to choose another. Settings, Credits, Study timer and Quit are also on the start menu. The current world name appears above the buttons. {{start-menu}}

rows: Go back from any sub-page to the first page.
Open the Study Grove focus timer (not while typing on the Worlds page).

items: [[Continue]] enters the current world.
[[Worlds]] lists your saved worlds and creates new ones (next section).
[[Settings]] opens the same settings panel you get in a world by pressing [[Esc]].

[[Credits]] shows seven title cards on a black stage: the maker, thanks and a dedication. Each card stays for 12 seconds and the set loops. Press [[Esc]], [[Enter]] or [[Space]], or choose **Skip credits**, to go back. There are no Previous or Next buttons yet. The normal music playlist keeps playing.

blocks.text: The first launch shows a tumbling wireframe cube while the world loads. Later loads show only a stage text and an activity bar.

items: Choose **Worlds** on the start menu.
Type a name. Typing both filters the list of saved worlds and names the world you are about to create.
Choose **Create world**, or press [[Enter]] while that row is selected.
Wait for the world to load; you arrive standing on the starting island.

blocks.text: New worlds always open in **creative** mode: there is no seed, mode or difficulty picker. Every new world's pack already holds 12 Berries, 2 Water flasks, 1 Empty flask and 4 Alder board pieces. {{new-world-start}}

The Worlds page shows only four rows at a time and the mouse wheel does not scroll it. Use the Up and Down arrows or type to filter. Rename, backups and thumbnails are not in the game yet. {{worlds-page}}

To keep a world near the top, click the star at the left of its row, or press [[Tab]] with the row selected. Starred worlds are listed right after the current world. Choose **Starred** (or press [[Shift]]+[[Tab]]) to show only starred worlds. Stars are saved in the worlds folder, not in the world.
To delete a world, hold its DELETE badge, or hold the [[Delete]] key with the row selected, for 3 seconds. The world you are currently in cannot be deleted.

Click the world once to capture the mouse. That first click never mines or places a block. While the mouse is released (after opening a panel, pressing [[Esc]], or switching away from the window) you cannot move or look. Closing a panel captures the mouse again on its own. {{mouse-capture}}

rows: Walk forward, left, back, right (about 4.3 m/s). You step up half-metre blocks without jumping.
Jump about 1.25 m; hold it to jump again on every landing. A full one-metre block needs a jump.
Sneak at about 1.3 m/s; you cannot walk off an edge while sneaking.
Crawl through gaps 0.6 m tall; press C or Space again to stand.
Start or stop flying (creative only). Space rises, Shift descends, Ctrl boosts.

blocks.text: Walking speeds do not depend on frame rate, because movement runs on a fixed 60 Hz step. {{walk-and-look}}
[[Print Screen]] releases the mouse so that you can use a system screenshot tool. The game itself has no screenshot key.

blocks.alt: First-person view over a flowering meadow with a few trees. A status message is at the top left, a square compass map at the top right with a small readout of frames per second and coordinates beneath it, a crosshair in the centre and a row of ten empty hotbar slots at the bottom.
blocks.caption: The in-game screen on a new creative world. Headless capture of the game at the audited commit (1280 × 720, fresh disposable world).

items: **Top left:** the status line. Actions report here, for example 'Collected … ×3' or 'Capacity full; block left behind'.
**Top right, left of the map:** the looking-at card, shown when you aim at a block within 6 m. [[F2]] hides or shows it, the same as Settings > General > Target info.
**Top right:** the compact map, with the FPS and coordinates box beneath it. The box is on by default; turn it off in Settings > Debug.
**Lower right:** the collection feed. It shows what you gained, for example '+3 Oak wood', for a few seconds. Crafting, creative mining and home storage do not show there.
**Middle:** the crosshair, and a small action hint under it.
**Lower left (survival only):** the four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina.
**Bottom:** the ten-slot hotbar and the label of the selected item.

blocks.text: Press [[F1]] to hide the whole HUD, the crosshair and your hands, for example before a screenshot; press it again to bring everything back. {{hud-layout}} {{clean-view}}

sections.title: Open your pack and the hotbar

blocks.alt: The inventory screen in creative mode. Tabs along the top read Pack, Craft, Build, Home and Journal. The Build tab is open and shows a paged grid of block icons with a search field and category buttons, and the hotbar of ten empty slots below.
blocks.caption: The inventory in creative mode with the Build tab open. Headless capture of the game at the audited commit (1280 × 720, fresh disposable world). This capture predates the capacity change: the header now reads 'Capacity: X / 1000'.

blocks.text: Press [[E]] to open the inventory and press it again to close it. The tabs are Pack, Craft, Home and Journal in survival, plus Build in creative; switch with the mouse, [[Tab]] or [[Shift]] + [[Tab]]. The header always shows how much you carry out of 1000 capacity. The Pack tab lists carried items as icons with quantity numbers; hover an icon to see its name. {{inventory-workspaces}}
The hotbar
The hotbar has ten slots that start empty. A slot is a shortcut to an item kind, not a container, so its number is everything of that kind in your pack.

rows: Bind that item to the slot (inventory open).
Drag an item onto a slot
Bind it. Dragging a slot onto another swaps them; dragging a slot off the bar clears it.

blocks.text: With the inventory closed, [[Tab]] cycles through the tools and weapons you carry and back to empty hands. Bindings are saved with the world. {{hotbar-quick-slots}}

There are exactly two modes. Press [[F4]] to switch, except on the start menu, in Study Grove or while connected to a server; your pack, hotbar and position stay as they are, and each world remembers the mode you left it in. {{game-modes}}
Creative

items: Blocks break instantly and placing is free; crafting is free.
The Build tab and catalog, middle-click block picking, building brushes and undo.
Flight, map travel and teleport.
Editable time, weather and season.

blocks.text: Survival

items: Blocks take time to mine and your pack is limited to 1000 capacity.
Four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina, shown lower left.
Falls hurt, and you eat with [[R]], drink with [[T]] and quick-craft with [[X]].
Dying returns you to your rest point and loses nothing.

blocks.text: Items you took from the creative catalog stay in your pack after you switch to survival. Continue with {{guide:first-survival-day|Your first survival day}}.

blocks.alt: The Paused settings panel with tabs General, Audio, World and Debug. Rows for field of view, horizon distance, mouse sensitivity, atmospheric fog, camera bob, frame limit, shader, GUI size and chunk fade-in are shown, with Resume, Main menu and Save and quit buttons at the bottom.
blocks.caption: The Paused panel opened with Esc. Headless capture of the game at the audited commit (1280 × 720, fresh disposable world).

blocks.text: Press [[Esc]] in the world to open Settings. The game pauses and the panel is titled 'Paused'. Esc first closes anything that is open (the pack, the large map, Study Grove), and only opens Settings when nothing is. The General tab also has Speed FOV (widens the view at high speed), Damage bob (Off, Reduced or Full camera dip when hurt) and Target info. {{settings-menu}} {{escape-and-pause}}

rows: Open Settings and release the mouse; press it again to close.
Save the world right now ('World saved safely').
Save and return to the start menu.
Ctrl + Q, Save & quit or the window's close button
Save, then quit. If saving fails, the game stays open.

blocks.text: The world also autosaves about every 30 seconds whenever it has unsaved changes. Settings are stored inside each world's save, so loading another world brings back that world's settings. {{saving-and-quitting}}

guides.title: Controls reference
guides.headline:
Every key,
and when it works.
guides.summary: The essential keys, the keys that change meaning with context, and a searchable list of every control in the audited game.
guides.lead: A short list of the keys you will use all the time, then every control the audit found, grouped by what you are doing and filterable by key or action.

verification.method: The full list below is generated from the feature ledger, so each row is the key and condition recorded in that ledger entry's source audit. The essentials table was checked against the same entries.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested. Keys cannot be rebound in this version of the game, so this list applies to everyone.

sections.title: The keys you will use most

rows: Walk. Fly horizontally in creative flight.
Look around, once you have clicked the world to capture the pointer.
Jump; rise while flying or swimming.
Sneak (ledge guard); also half-metre pieces, diving, descending and steadying a ranged weapon.
Mine or remove the block you aim at; hit an animal.
Place the held block (a block selected, no tool equipped); hold to draw a bow or wind up a throw.
Equip the next tool (inventory closed) or the next inventory tab (inventory open).
Close what is open, or open Settings.

blocks.text: Hold Shift while mining or placing to work on a single half-metre piece instead of a whole block. Logs and cactus are always felled as a whole tree or stem.

items: **Shift** is shared: sneak on the ground, half-metre mining and placing, dive in water, descend while flying, and steadier aim with a bow or rifle. {{sneak-ledge-guard}}
**Tab** equips tools when the inventory is closed and switches tabs when it is open. {{equip-tools-tab}}
**Z** zooms, but **Ctrl + Z** is undo in creative, so Z does not zoom while Ctrl is held. {{hold-to-zoom}}
**C** crawls on foot. In a boat, it cycles camera stations. {{crawl}}
**F** toggles flight in creative; in survival it only shows 'Flight is available in creative mode'. {{creative-flight}}
**F5** cycles first person, third person rear and third person front. The perspective is not saved. {{camera-perspectives}}

blocks.text: On a non-QWERTY keyboard every key above is read by position. Use the key where it sits on a QWERTY board. {{input-devices-and-layout}}
Each row names the feature that owns it; follow the link for its summary and source evidence. Rows for developer tools or features still in development carry a status label.

guides.title: Your first survival day
guides.headline:
Your first survival day,
from berries to a home.
guides.summary: Switch to survival, read the four bars, drink, eat, mine, make stone tools, cook, build a home and avoid the real dangers.
guides.lead: What the four bars mean, what to do in the first minutes, which crafting chain gets you tools and a roof, and what can actually hurt you.

verification.method: Meter timings, damage values, recipe counts and key behaviours come from the game source at the audited commit and its own unit tests, each traced to a ledger entry.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested. The numbers describe this version: planned food plants, furnaces and ground items would change this guide.

blocks.text: New worlds begin in creative. Press [[F4]] to switch; you keep your pack, hotbar and position, and the four bars appear lower left. Every new world's pack holds 12 Berries, 2 Water flasks, 1 Empty flask and 4 Alder board pieces, and switching modes or respawning never grants more. {{new-world-start}}
Items you took from the creative catalog before switching stay in your pack, so start in a fresh world if you want a true first day.

rows: Health. It regenerates slowly while both hunger and thirst stay above 65.
A full bar lasts about 40 minutes.
A full bar lasts about 30 minutes.
Spent by sprinting, which needs more than 3% left. Resting at home refills it.

blocks.text: The bars do not change in creative. The starter pack is good for roughly 24 minutes of food and 21 minutes of water, which the Home tab's trip readout will tell you. {{survival-meters}} {{trip-preparation-readout}}

rows: Drink (+22 thirst) and refill every Empty flask you carry.
Drink one carried Water flask (+35 thirst); you keep the Empty flask.
Eat one food: Berries first, then Venison, Raw meat, and Cooked meat last.
Click a food in the Pack
Eat it. Click a Water flask to drink, the same as T. Within reach of water, that refills your empty flasks instead of drinking.

blocks.text: Only four foods exist. Berries come only from the starter pack, so the renewable food is hunting, best cooked over charcoal (below). Fruit blocks and Date clusters are building blocks, not food. {{eating}} {{drinking-flasks}}

Hold left click on a block within 6 m. A progress bar fills and the whole one-metre block, up to eight pieces, goes straight into your pack. Hold [[Shift]] to take a single half-metre piece of any block except a log or cactus. Logs and cactus fell the whole connected tree or stem instead, and Shift does not change that. Nothing drops on the ground: if the pieces do not fit, the block stays where it is and the status line says 'Capacity full; block left behind'. {{mining-harvesting}}

Your pack is limited by capacity, 1000, not by slots. {{carry-capacity}} Any block can be mined by hand; a tool only speeds up its own material: the pickaxe about 4× on rock, glass and masonry, the hatchet about 3.6× on logs, boards and leaves, the shovel about 3.4× on loose ground. {{mining-speed-tools}}
Water and other liquids cannot be collected.

items: Mine a log piece from a tree and open the inventory with [[E]], then the **Craft** tab.
Choose one of the 'Split … boards' recipes: one log piece makes four board pieces.
Mine stone blocks; any of the 26 natural stones counts.
Craft a Stone hatchet, Stone pickaxe or Stone shovel, then the sword if you want to hunt. Crafting a tool equips it automatically.

blocks.text: There is a single tool tier, and tools never wear out. There is no workbench: everything is crafted from the Craft tab. {{stone-tools}}

Do not press [[X]] to quick-craft with the starter kit. It crafts the first affordable recipe in list order, so with only boards in your pack it burns your four boards into two Charcoal. {{quick-craft-x}}

Animals never attack you. Left click one to hit it: a bare hand or ordinary tool deals 12 damage and the Stone sword deals 28. In survival what it drops goes straight into your pack; drops that do not fit are lost. {{melee-attacks}} {{animal-drops}}
Fire work is crafting, not a placed furnace or campfire: it works anywhere. Raw meat restores 8 hunger and Cooked meat 30, and one Venison roasts into two Cooked meat. {{fire-and-glass-chain}}

items: Stand on dry, solid ground, open the **Home** tab and choose **Establish home**. It costs 8 board pieces and places a small crate 1.5 m beside you.
Move items to and from the crate by clicking rows in the Home tab; it holds up to 400 capacity while you are within 6 m. Shift + click moves as many as fit.
Build a roof with cover on at least two sides next to the crate, then choose **Rest / set respawn** there.

blocks.text: Resting sets your respawn point and refills stamina; it does not heal or feed you. Leaves and tree trunks count as cover, plants and water do not. {{home-crate}} {{rest-respawn-point}}

items: **Falls:** up to 3 m is free, each extra metre costs 5 HP, so about 23 m is fatal from full health. Only landing on solid ground counts. {{fall-damage-hazards}}
**Starvation and thirst** when the bars run empty.
**Extreme cold** only at very high altitude, and **explosions**. No drowning, lava, fire or hostile animals exist in this version.
**Death** respawns you at once at your rest point (the world's start until you rest at home) and you lose nothing. {{death-respawn}}

blocks.text: Body temperature is never shown and, with this version's numbers, heat damage cannot happen. {{temperature-shelter}}

Planting and growing food, a placeable furnace with smelting and metal tools, visible items on the ground, a larger pack and achievements are planned but absent from this version. They are tracked in the {{planned-planting-food-plants|feature ledger}} and will get their own guide only after they ship.

guides.title: Crafting and recipes
guides.headline:
Crafting,
all 43 recipes.
guides.summary: How the Craft tab works, which ingredients can be mixed, the quick-craft trap, and the complete recipe list with amounts.
guides.lead: There is no workbench: every recipe is crafted from the pack. This guide explains the panel and lists every recipe with its exact amounts.

verification.method: The recipe tables are generated from data/recipes.json, which was extracted from the game's recipe registry at Voxelgame fb873488 (the other features are still from the audited commit dd29d91); tools/validate_guides.py can recheck all 43 names, sections and amounts against a source snapshot.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested. Amounts are carried pieces: 8 pieces make one full one-metre block. Recipes for furnaces, smelting and metal tools do not exist yet.

blocks.text: Open the inventory with [[E]] and choose **Craft**. Recipes are grouped into four sections: Timber, Fire & food, Materials and Tools & arms. Each ingredient shows as carried / required. Everything is crafted anywhere, with no workbench, fire or furnace. {{crafting-panel}}

rows: Left / Right arrows, or click a section
Enter or C, or click Craft
Shift + Enter, Shift + C or Shift + click
Craft repeatedly until materials or space run out (at most 256 batches).

items: In survival the ingredients are spent and the result needs room in the pack. Failures read 'Missing materials for …' or 'Not enough free carry capacity'.
In creative the ingredients are free ('Creative: ingredients are free').
A crafted tool is equipped at once and a crafted boat is selected.
You cannot open the inventory while inside a vehicle.

blocks.text: Counts are half-metre pieces. One full one-metre block is 8 pieces, so a recipe that needs 8 of a material needs one block of it.
A few ingredients accept a whole group of materials, and you can mix the members freely. {{ingredient-groups}}

items: **Boards:** any species (Alder, Birch or Pine).
**Natural stone:** any of 26 natural stones.
**Hardwood or deadwood:** any hardwood log or deadwood.
**Plant fiber or Wool.**

blocks.text: Every other ingredient must be that exact material: Sand (not other sands), Clay (not ochre, umber, sienna, cracked or banded clay), Reeds (not Tall reeds), Limestone, Granite, Cobblestone, Moss, Chalk, Basalt, Red rock, Glass, Feather, Raw meat, Venison and Glow crystal.

Not usable as natural stone: Magma stone, Iron ore, Bog iron, Amethyst, Salt, Sulfur crust, Mineral crust, Geyser stone and any crafted masonry. Sandstone is the exception: it counts as natural stone, although you can also craft it from sand.
With the inventory closed, [[X]] crafts the first recipe you can currently afford, in list order, not the recipe you last selected. In creative it only shows a message. {{quick-craft-x}}
The list starts with the four log-splitting recipes and then 'Burn a charcoal pile'. With boards but no logs, X turns four boards into two Charcoal.

Fire work is crafting, not a placed furnace: burn 4 boards into 2 Charcoal, then spend Charcoal to cook meat, fire Sand into Glass, blow Glass into flasks, and fire clay, limestone and lacquer. Fill flasks by pressing [[T]] at water. {{fire-and-glass-chain}}
Besides the 'Fire glass' recipe, the Survey workshop landmark's one-time find gives 8 Glass.

Cutting a log on a natural tree, or a cactus stem, brings down that piece and everything growing from it. Cut the bottom log to take the whole tree. Cut a branch and the trunk below it stays standing. {{tree-felling}}

items: In survival the chop takes as long as all the wood and leaves it removes together. All of it goes into your pack.
If the whole harvest does not fit, the status line says 'Need X capacity free to collect this connected tree' and nothing is cut.
A log you placed yourself breaks like any other block, one piece at a time.
A finished tree reports 'Felled a tree' with the number of logs and leaves.

blocks.text: Shores mix Clay (below sea level), Gravel and Sand. Desert ground is Sand. Reeds grow in wetlands. Wild flax grows in some meadows of worlds made with the current generator. Feathers, wool and meat come from animals. {{material-sources}}
Older worlds have no Wild flax, so use Wool for bindings there.
The Pack tab lists everything you carry. Tools come first, then food and drink, blocks, materials and spawn eggs. Each group is sorted by name. {{pack-items-list}}

rows: Use it, select it or equip it. A material with no use says it is stored as a crafting resource.
Hover an item, then press 1-9 or 0
Bind it to that hotbar slot.
Drag an item onto a hotbar slot
Bind it to that slot while the inventory is open.
Switch between the item list and a turning character portrait.

blocks.text: Hover an item to see its name, quantity, category and click hints. The side panel turns the item in 3D and shows what it is for, where it comes from, which recipe uses it, and how much pack room one piece takes. {{item-info-previews}}
'USED IN' shows only the first recipe that names the exact item. Some stones count through the natural-stone group, so their panel can say 'USE: PLACE / BUILD' even when a recipe accepts them.
The block table at Voxelgame f3143de9 has 180 block types, not counting Air. Each has its own name and colour. Recipes on this page name the blocks they use. {{block-materials-catalogue}}

items: Six block types are water: Water, Hot spring water, Dark fjord water, Fresh water, Black water and Boiling water.
Iron ore and Bog iron can be mined and placed. No recipe uses them, and the game has no smelting yet.
Glow crystal is the gem that recipes use. It does not generate naturally; see the section on recipes survival cannot finish yet.

blocks.text: Every recipe in this version, in the order the Craft tab shows them. Each makes the stated amount from the stated inputs in one craft.

Red lantern, Alder rifle, Four rifle rounds, TNT and Two dynamite sticks each need Glow crystal, which does not generate naturally in the world, so a survival player cannot gather enough. They work in creative, or in survival with crystals carried over from creative by pressing [[F4]]. {{lumen-crystal-supply}}
A placeable furnace or campfire, smelting, metal tools and tool durability are planned and have no recipes in this version.

guides.title: Install, update and find your worlds
guides.headline:
Install the game,
keep your worlds.
guides.summary: Install Voxelgame on Linux, Windows or macOS, update it by running the installer again, and find the folders that hold your worlds.
guides.lead: Each installer builds the game from the source folder and adds a launcher. Worlds and settings live in a separate data folder, so an update leaves them alone.

verification.method: Installer steps, folder names and world file rules come from the installer scripts and the save code at the audited commit, each traced to a ledger entry. Each ledger entry lists its source lines.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested. Linux is the platform the installer is tested on. Windows and macOS are marked Limited because no real machine has validated them yet.

blocks.text: You need an internet connection, several GB of free disk space and a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux the game runs in an X11 or XWayland session; it has no native Wayland window.
Keep the extracted source folder until setup finishes. You can delete it afterwards.

items: Open a terminal in the extracted source folder.
Run **bash install.sh** as your normal user. Do not use sudo; setup only uses it for system packages.
Read the plan and confirm it. Setup installs compiler and audio tools with apt-get, dnf or pacman, installs Rust, builds the game and adds Voxelgame to your application menu.
Start Voxelgame from the application menu.

rows: Install the app into another folder
Skip the tool install; use this on other distributions after installing the tools yourself (see docs/INSTALLING.md)

blocks.text: Setup never starts the game and never touches existing worlds.
The Windows installer has not been tested on a real Windows PC yet.

items: Double-click **install-windows.cmd**.
Confirm the plan. If Windows asks, approve the Microsoft C++ Build Tools installer.
Wait while setup downloads any missing Build Tools, Rust and FFmpeg, then builds the game.
Start Voxelgame from the Start menu. The shortcut has no Voxelgame icon.

blocks.text: If the compiler setup asks you to restart Windows, restart it and run the installer again. Managed PCs may need an administrator to allow PowerShell scripts. In PowerShell, run **install-windows.ps1** with the same options as the Linux installer: -Yes or -Prefix PATH.
The macOS build is not validated yet. Graphics and sound are untested, and the game may fail to start on some Macs.

items: Double-click **Install-macOS.command** and press Return to accept the plan.
If Apple offers the Command Line Tools installer, finish it.
If Homebrew asks for your password, enter your Mac password.
Open Voxelgame.app from the Applications folder in your home folder.

blocks.text: The app is unsigned and not notarized. If macOS blocks it, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway. You can also run **bash install.sh** in Terminal. Do not turn off Gatekeeper.
On some Macs the F4 mode key needs Fn+F4.
There is no separate updater. Install a newer version the same way you installed the first one.

items: Close the game. [[Ctrl+Q]] saves and quits.
Extract the newer source folder.
Run its installer again: **bash install.sh**, **Install-macOS.command** or **install-windows.cmd**.
Your worlds and settings stay in the data folder.
If the build fails, the old version keeps working.
The launcher switches to the new version only after the new copy is complete.
Setup does not delete old versions. Delete the older folders in the app's versions folder yourself, after you have checked the new version.

blocks.text: Going back to an older build is not supported. It may fail to open worlds saved by a newer build.

rows: Worlds and settings: ~/Library/Application Support/Voxelgame. Installer logs: ~/Library/Logs/Voxelgame

blocks.text: Setup writes a log once it starts, including runs that fail later. It prints the log path at the start, and a failed run does not repeat it. A stop before setup starts, such as a cancelled plan, leaves no log. Its file name is install-<date>-<id>.log. On Linux and macOS, set VOXELGAME_INSTALL_LOG_DIR to change the log folder.

items: Each world is one .vxw file in the worlds folder inside the data folder.
Stars from the Worlds page are kept in worlds/favourites.txt, one save path per line, not inside the world file.
The starting world is worlds/debug/debug.vxw. The menu lists it as DEBUG.

A world with a name is saved in a folder named from the name in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, for example worlds/my-island/world.vxw. If that folder already exists, a number is added (my-island-2). A name with no usable letters or numbers gets a numbered folder.
A world with an empty name is saved as worlds/world-0001/world.vxw, then world-0002, and so on.

blocks.text: The game stores only your changes. Untouched terrain is generated again from the world's seed. New worlds have no seed field.
Continue opens the starting world

The starting world is always worlds/debug/debug.vxw, so Continue opens DEBUG after every restart. To keep playing another world, open Worlds and load it. Settings are saved per world. The settings you see right after launch belong to DEBUG.
Close the game before you copy a world file, so the copy holds the latest save. Autosave runs about every 30 seconds after world changes such as building, mining, storage, journal edits or boats.

The installer does not move worlds from a source checkout started with ./run.sh. Copying that worlds folder into the data folder with the game closed should work, but this is inferred from the save paths and has not been tested.

Linux with a Vulkan graphics driver and an X11 or XWayland session is the tested platform. The Windows (64-bit Intel or AMD, Windows 10 or 11) and macOS (Apple Silicon, or Intel with a Metal GPU) installers are included, but no real machine has checked graphics and sound on them yet. {{system-requirements}}
The first build needs internet access and several GB of free disk space. The README's 60 FPS target assumes at least an integrated GPU. Software Vulkan (llvmpipe) is only for diagnostics.
There is no uninstaller. Delete the app folder and its launcher by hand. {{uninstall}}

items: **Linux:** delete the app folder, `~/.local/share/voxelgame/app` by default, and `~/.local/share/applications/voxelgame.desktop`.
**macOS:** delete `~/Applications/Voxelgame.app`.
**Windows:** delete the app folder and the Voxelgame shortcut in your Start menu Programs folder. The FFmpeg copy in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\tools` stays unless you delete it too.
Compilers, Rust, Homebrew and audio tools that setup installed stay on the PC.

blocks.text: Your worlds stay in the data folder until you delete it. Deleting the data folder removes all worlds for good, so copy any world you want to keep first.
Developers can build the game without the installer. With Rust 1.75 or newer and the Linux packages installed, run `cargo run --release --locked --bin voxelgame`, or `./run.sh`. {{build-from-source}}

items: `run.sh` rebuilds only when sources, assets or Cargo files are newer than the program. It shows a small Preparing the game window while it builds.
Started this way, worlds live in the worlds folder inside the source folder.
Optional: `aplay` (alsa-utils) for sound and `ffmpeg` for music.

blocks.text: The Linux menu entry and the macOS app use the Voxelgame cube icon. The Windows Start menu shortcut and the game window have no icon. {{app-icon}}

guides.title: Fixing startup, sound and save problems
guides.headline:
Fix startup,
sound and saves.
guides.summary: Find the error message, check your graphics driver and sound players, and recover a world that will not load.
guides.lead: Most startup failures print their reason to a terminal. Start the game from a terminal first, then use the matching section below.

verification.method: Error text, file paths, keys and save rules come from the game and installer source at the audited commit. Each ledger entry lists its source lines.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested on every platform. Linux is the platform the installer is tested on. Windows and macOS graphics and sound are marked Limited because no real machine has validated them yet.

blocks.text: When the game cannot start, it closes and prints the reason to the terminal. Menu and desktop launches show no error window, so start Voxelgame from a terminal to read the message.

items: **voxelgame could not start: ...** means a bad option was given. The game exits with code 2.
**voxelgame failed: ...** means any other startup failure. The game exits with code 1.

blocks.text: Messages you may see:

items: **no Vulkan-compatible graphics adapter found**: the graphics driver is missing. See Graphics driver problems below.
**GPU ran out of memory during startup**: lower **Settings > General > Horizon distance**, then try again.
**Nearby terrain took too long to prepare; please try again**: shown on the main menu. Try again, or lower **Settings > General > Horizon distance**.
**audio disabled: playback command unavailable**: sound players are missing. See Sound and music below.

blocks.text: Setup failures are written to an installer log. See {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}}.
Problems with other worlds appear on the main menu instead of closing the game.
The game never overwrites a world file it cannot read. The file stays as it is, so you can move it or try again later.
A world from the Worlds list fails
The main menu shows **world could not be loaded: ...** and you stay where you were. Pick another world or fix the file, then try again.
The starting world fails

The game opens the starting world, `worlds/debug/debug.vxw`, or the file named by `VOXELGAME_SAVE_PATH` when you start it. If that file cannot be read, the game closes before the main menu and prints the reason to the terminal.

items: Close the game.
Move the damaged `.vxw` file to a backup folder. Do not delete it.
Start the game again. A new starting world is created when the file is missing.

blocks.text: Moving the file aside means the game starts with a new starting world. Keep the old file if you may want its contents back. Find the data folder with {{guide:install-and-worlds|Install, update and find your worlds}}.

Press **F6** in a world to save now. The game also saves when you choose **Main menu** or **Save & quit** in the Esc menu, press **Ctrl+Q**, close the window, or load or create another world. Autosave runs every 30 seconds when the world has changed.
Autosave runs after changes such as building, mining, home storage, journal edits or boats. Walking around and most crafting wait for the next F6 or quit, so press F6 after a long crafting session.
If saving fails while you quit, the game stays open. Fix the cause, such as a full disk, and save again.
There is no crash recovery. A crash loses changes made since the last save. The previous save file is kept intact.
Voxelgame needs a working Vulkan graphics driver. On Linux it runs in an X11 or XWayland session. It has no native Wayland window.

items: **Debian and Fedora**: the installer adds Mesa Vulkan drivers.
**Arch**: install **vulkan-intel** or **vulkan-radeon**, or your NVIDIA driver.
**macOS**: a Metal-capable GPU is required.

blocks.text: The game picks your high-performance GPU first. If that fails, it falls back to a software renderer such as llvmpipe. The fallback is useful for diagnosis but too slow for normal play.
To reduce GPU load, set **Settings > General > Horizon distance** lower, turn off **Settings > Debug > Distant terrain**, or set **Settings > General > Shader** to **None**.
Windows graphics have not been validated on a real Windows PC yet.
Sound effects need a player program: **aplay** from alsa-utils on Linux, or **ffplay** on Windows and macOS. The installers set these up. Without a player the game runs silently.
Music also needs **ffmpeg** to decode the songs. Song files may be mp3, ogg, wav or flac.

items: If ffmpeg is missing, Music turns itself off and the status line shows **Music unavailable: ...**.
After you install ffmpeg, open **Settings > Audio** and switch Music back on.

sections.title: Record lag spikes for a bug report

blocks.text: With the Performance overlay (F3) on, a frame that takes at least 25 ms and more than twice your frame budget is written to a log. Turn F3 off to stop recording. {{lag-spike-log}}

items: **Linux:** `~/.local/state/voxelgame/lag-spikes.jsonl`, or inside `$XDG_STATE_HOME/voxelgame` if that variable is set.
Each entry has the world seed, your position, the frame cost and up to eight of the slowest causes.

blocks.text: The F3 panel shows the log status: armed, recording, dropped or unavailable. Attach the file when you report a slow frame.

guides.title: Hunting, weapons and animals
guides.headline:
Hunt with a sword,
bow, rifle or rock.
guides.summary: Animals never attack. Learn the melee, throwing, bow and rifle controls, and what each kill gives you.
guides.lead: Hunting is the renewable food in survival. No animal fights back, so the only hard part is getting close enough and keeping the weapon ready.

verification.method: Controls, damage, draw times and drop rules come from the game source at the audited commit. Each ledger entry lists its source lines.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. Draw, wind-up and reload times are the code values; check them in play if they feel different.

blocks.text: Every animal is passive. None of them attack, chase or damage you. Farm animals stay calm near you. Small wild animals, such as rabbits and foxes, keep their distance and run when you come close. Any animal runs for a few seconds after you hurt it. {{no-hostile-mobs}} {{animal-behaviour}}
There is no taming, riding, breeding, feeding, milking or shearing.

sections.title: Hit with a hand, tool or sword

items: Get within reach of the animal and aim at it.
Left-click to hit it.
A hurt animal runs off for a few seconds. Chase it and hit it again.

blocks.text: A bare hand or an ordinary tool deals 12 damage. The Stone sword deals 28. In creative, one hit removes the animal and gives you nothing. Tall grass or flowers between you and the animal can block the hit. {{melee-attacks}}

rows: Wind up. A full wind-up takes 0.7 s.
Throw. A wind-up that is too short is cancelled.

blocks.text: Harder throws fly farther and hit harder. Each throw uses one rock in survival. Rocks hurt animals only, not you or vehicles. {{throwing-rocks}}

items: Craft an Alder bow and some arrows.
Equip the bow. Press [[Tab]] or [[Shift]] + [[Tab]] to cycle through what you carry.
Hold right click to draw. A full draw takes 0.85 s.
Release to shoot. Letting go before about a fifth of a draw cancels the shot.

blocks.text: Longer draws fly faster and hit harder. In survival each shot uses one arrow, and arrows are not recovered. Arrows stop on grass, flowers and other small plants. Creative arrows are unlimited. {{alder-bow}}
The reed versions use reeds instead of wool or plant fiber for the string and shafts, so you do not need animal drops for them.

rows: Raise the sights for less spread and sway. You cannot aim while it reloads.
Does not reload the rifle. In survival, R eats food instead.

blocks.text: The rifle reloads itself about one second after every shot. Survival uses one rifle round per shot; creative is unlimited. Rounds hurt animals and vehicles. {{alder-rifle}}

sections.title: What you get from a kill

blocks.text: In survival, drops go straight into your pack. Meat and venison are food, feathers make arrows, and wool can replace plant fiber. Hide has no use yet. If your pack is full, drops that do not fit are lost, because there are no items on the ground. Creative kills give nothing. {{animal-drops}}
Cook meat over charcoal before you eat it. Cooked meat restores much more hunger than raw meat. See {{guide:first-survival-day|Your first survival day}} for the hunger numbers.

guides.title: Seasons and the look of the world
guides.headline:
Seasons change
how the world looks.
guides.summary: A year lasts 80 minutes. Each season changes colours and light. Blocks, building and tools stay the same. Snow and thinner leaves are planned, not in the game yet.
guides.lead: The season changes how the world looks. It does not change the air temperature in survival. Nothing you build, mine or walk on changes with it.

verification.method: Season length, the colours each season changes, the temperature values and the Settings > World rows come from the game source at the audited commit. The air temperature rules were read from the code at commit 150cd60 (rain only, no season term), not measured in play.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. Season colours are described in words because no season screenshots exist yet.

blocks.text: A full year lasts 80 real minutes, so each season lasts about 20 minutes. New worlds start in summer. The order is spring, summer, autumn and winter, then back to spring. {{seasons}}
Each season changes the colours of grass, deciduous leaves, needles, blossoms and water. The sky and sunlight change too: autumn leaves turn russet, and winter light is cooler.

items: Press [[Esc]] and open the World tab in Settings.
Click a Season chip, or use its arrows, to hold Spring, Summer, Autumn or Winter.
Choose Auto to go back to the normal cycle.

blocks.text: The Season row reads AUTO / and the current season while the cycle runs. If a creative player fixed the season, the row shows that season instead. In survival you cannot change the row. {{creative-world-controls}}

In survival the air temperature does not depend on the season. Time of day adds up to 9 C at midday and takes up to 4.5 C off at night. Rain lowers it by up to 2 C. Altitude also lowers it, by about 1 C for every 40 blocks above sea level. {{day-night-cycle}} {{automatic-weather}}

Your body temperature follows the air. It costs health only while it is outside -12 to 48 C. At sea level the air stays between about 9.5 and 25 C, so heat does not hurt you there. Higher ground is colder. A roof and walls pull your temperature toward 20 C. {{temperature-shelter}}
The Home tab shows the current air temperature on its Temperature line, so you can check it before a long trip.

sections.title: What the season does not change

items: No snow falls and no snow blocks appear.
Trees keep all their blocks. Leaves do not thin out.
Weather follows its own pattern, not the season.
The season does not change which animals appear or what crafting needs.

sections.title: Planned, not in the game yet

blocks.text: Planned: leaves that thin out on some trees, and grass that looks snowy in winter. Until these ship, the game works as described above.

guides.title: Maps and finding your way back
guides.headline:
Mark it, find it,
get back to it.
guides.summary: Use the compact and fullscreen maps, the biome locator, Journal places and destinations. Keep a build easy to find after a long trip.
guides.lead: Two maps show the generated terrain. You can mark places, set a destination and search for biomes. Your own builds are not drawn on the maps, so save a place before you travel far.

verification.method: Keys, limits and map behaviour come from the feature ledger, which cites the game source lines for each entry. Map sizes, zoom range, the 16-place Journal limit and the 320 m beacon are code values.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. Compare the zoom steps and the beacon height with what you see in play.

blocks.text: The compact map is a small north-up view in the top-right corner. It shows about 128 m around you and is on by default. The fullscreen map covers 512 m at first and can zoom out to about 131 km. {{compact-map}} {{fullscreen-map}}

rows: Show or hide the compact map.
Open or close the fullscreen map.

blocks.text: The maps show generated terrain only. Blocks you place or dig do not appear on them.

items: Press Shift + M to open the map. When you play offline, the world pauses while it is open. On a server, the world keeps running.
Scroll the mouse wheel over the map to zoom in or out.
Drag with the left mouse button to look around. Dragging does not move you.
Press BACK TO PLAYER in the side panel to centre the map on you again.

blocks.text: The readout under the map shows the X and Z position under the cursor and its distance from you. With the cursor off the map, it shows the map centre. {{map-player-marker}} Your position is a gold arrow that points the way you face.

items: Open the fullscreen map.
Right-click the spot you want. The game adds a pin named Marker 1, Marker 2 and so on, and sets it as your destination.
Right-click an existing pin to remove it.

blocks.text: Markers use the same 16-place limit as the Journal. Rename them in the Journal to give them a clear name. {{map-right-click-markers}}
Right-clicking a pin removes it even when it is a named Journal place. If the game says the Journal is full, remove a place first.

items: Press E, then Tab to reach the Journal. You can also click the Journal button on the fullscreen map.
Type a name and an optional note in the Name and Note fields. Press Enter to finish typing.
Click Pin this location to save the spot where you stand. A blank name becomes Place 1, Place 2 and so on.
Click a place to select it, make it your destination, or change its text. Click Save selected note to keep the changes.

blocks.text: The Journal holds 16 places and lists each one with its distance from you. Use Prev and Next to page through them. Places are saved per world. {{journal-places}}
The destination is the place the maps and the screen point to. It can be a map marker, a Journal place or an expedition site. {{destination-beacon}}

items: On both maps it shows as an amber +.
In the world it shows as an amber light column about 320 m tall.
On screen it shows as a gold diamond with the name and distance. The diamond sticks to the screen edge when the place is out of view. It reads HERE within 3 m.

blocks.text: There is no clear button. Pick another place to change the destination, or remove the selected place to clear it. With no destination, the maps show your home crate as a + instead. {{home-crate}}

items: Open the fullscreen map and click the search field on the left.
Type a name, such as crystal, meteorite, caldera or lava tunnel. The list filters as you type.
Press Enter, or click a result. The map centres on the first match, highlights it in cyan and drops a pin with the distance and coordinates.
Press FIND NEXT to search outward for another match, or CLEAR to remove the pin and highlight.

blocks.text: The locator does not move you. Pan the map first if you want to search from another spot, because the search starts at the map centre. {{map-locator}} The list includes Volcano, Cliff island, Mountain range and all 92 biomes.
In creative you can jump to a place from the map. Survival maps are a chart only.

items: Click a spot on the fullscreen map without dragging. You land on a clear spot there.
Or click the COORDINATES field, type X Z, or X Y Z for an exact height, and press Enter or TELEPORT.

blocks.text: Teleporting does not save where you came from, and there is no go back button. Save a Journal place before you jump. You must leave a vehicle or boat helm first. {{map-click-travel}} {{map-coordinate-teleport}}
In survival, clicking the map only shows a reminder. Zooming, dragging, the locator and markers still work. {{survival-map-chart}}

The small readout at the top right shows FPS, your X, Y and Z in metres, and your biome. It is on by default. Turn it off in Settings > Debug with FPS and coordinates. It is hidden while a panel is open. {{position-readout}}

items: North is -Z and east is +X.
Write the numbers down before a long trip. They are the same numbers the coordinates field uses.

sections.title: Get back to a lost build

items: Stand at the build and open the Journal. Type a name in the Name box, then press Pin this location. To rename a place, select it, edit the name and press Save selected note.
Before you travel far, open the fullscreen map and check the place shows as a pin.
To return, select the place in the Journal and make it your destination. Then follow the beacon or the diamond.

blocks.text: The maps show terrain, not your builds. A destination pin is the way back when a build is hard to recognise in the terrain.

guides.title: Building basics and creative tools
guides.headline:
Place it, shape it,
undo the mistakes.
guides.summary: Place whole blocks and half-metre pieces, use the creative brushes, copy and paste, and undo your work.
guides.lead: A whole block is a 1 m cube. Hold Shift to work with half-metre pieces. In creative mode, the brushes build lines, walls, floors and copies in one action, and Ctrl+Z undoes your last building action.

verification.method: Controls, brush order, limits and undo rules come from the feature ledger, which cites the game source for each entry (building.rs, game/building.rs, game.rs). Brush sizes and the 512-piece limit are code values. Middle-click picking, water and placement refusals come from the ledger rows middle-click-pick, building-in-water and placement-restrictions, checked at Voxelgame 5a69dce2 (game.rs middle-click handler, world/raycast.rs, world/block.rs replaceable(), game/readouts.rs placement_preview, game/mod_vehicles.rs block_interaction_available, save.rs MAX_EDITS).
verification.limits: Source-checked at 5a69dce2, not play-tested in this guide. Water and the 200,000-edit limit were read from code only. The structure library (naming, O, pictures) was checked at 9f915bcb, not play-tested.

items: Select a block in the hotbar with keys 1 to 0, or pick it from the Build catalog in creative.
Aim at the face where you want the block. A ghost shows the cell it will fill.
Right-click to place one block. The held item must be a block. With a bow, rifle or throwing rock in hand, right-click aims or throws instead.

blocks.text: A whole block is eight half-metre pieces. In survival, each whole block uses 8 pieces of that material from your pack, and the game says so if you are short. Creative placement is free. {{whole-block-placement}}
If any part of the target cell is occupied, the whole block is refused and the outline turns red. You cannot place a block inside yourself. Plants and water in the target cell are overwritten.

In creative, middle-click the block you aim at to pick it. If the block is already in a hotbar slot, that slot is selected. Otherwise the block is held without changing your other slots. Aiming at a door picks the closed door. Middle-click does nothing in survival. {{middle-click-pick}}

Your aim passes through water to the first solid block. Stand on the shore and aim at a lake or sea bed, then build up from it. You cannot click the water surface itself. Placed blocks replace water and plants in their cell. {{building-in-water}}
A block is refused, with a message in the status line, when:

items: Only blocks can be placed. Tools, food and other items cannot.
Your hands are empty, or a tool, bow, rifle or throwing rock is in hand.
A solid block is in the target cell.
In survival, your pack does not have 8 pieces of the material for a whole block.
The world already holds 200,000 changed blocks. New building is refused, and the save warns before the limit. {{placement-restrictions}}

blocks.text: The Water block in the creative catalog is a flowing source. Right-click with Water selected to place one. It spreads up to 7 half-metre cells sideways and pours down over edges. Flowing water does not go away on its own. {{flowing-water}}

items: Placing a block into water replaces that water cell.
Digging next to the sea or a lake lets water flow into the new gap.
Survival players cannot pick up or place water. There are no buckets.
The other five water types are blocks. They do not flow.

blocks.text: To stop unwanted flowing water, fill each wet cell with blocks. On a multiplayer server the server runs the water.

Hold Shift to work on one half-metre piece instead of a whole cube. Use it for half steps, thin walls, trim and carving. There are no slabs, stairs or sloped blocks; you build those shapes from pieces. {{half-metre-detail-building}} {{block-targeting-feedback}}

rows: Carve one half-metre piece from a block. Logs and cactus still fell the whole tree or stem.
Clean view. Hides the outline, ghost and HUD while you play.

blocks.text: Holding Shift also sneaks on foot, dives in water and descends while flying.
Doors are built from boards. A small door is one metre wide and two metres tall, with one leaf. A wide door is two metres wide and three metres tall, with two one-metre leaves. {{doors}}

items: **Wooden door:** one block of boards. Craft it in the Timber section.
**Wide wooden door:** two blocks of boards.
Hold the door and right click solid ground to hang it. The spot needs free space and solid ground under it.
Right click a hung door to open it, and right click again to close it. A door swings away from the player who opens it, from either side.
The leaves turn on their hinges over 0.35 seconds, easing in and settling gently. Using a door again while it is moving turns it back from where it stands.
A door will not open if anything other than air, water or plants is in its swing path. It also will not open while you or an animal stands where the leaves sweep. Clear the space and try again.
An open leaf stands a metre out of the doorway. You and walking animals cannot walk through it, and you cannot place a block into the space it stands in.
You cannot close a door while you stand in its opening. Step out first. A door will not shut while an animal stands in its opening.

Hitting the door itself takes the whole door down. In survival it goes back into your pack if there is room; if the pack is full, it is left hanging. Mining a block next to an open leaf leaves the door standing.

blocks.text: Doors cannot be hung or opened on a server yet. Blueprints skip door leaves, so a door is not copied.
A wooden chest is one metre cube of storage. It keeps items where you set it down, so you can leave things at a build site. {{wooden-chests}}

items: **Wooden chest:** one block of boards. Craft it in the Timber section.
Hold the chest and right click to set it down. It fills the metre cell under the ghost, with the latch toward you.
Right click a chest within 6 m to open its Chest tab. Your pack and the chest sit side by side.
Click an item to move one across. Shift+click moves all of that item.
A chest holds up to 250 capacity and up to 64 kinds of item.
To take a chest up, break it. In survival it goes back into your pack with everything inside, but only if the pack has room for all of it. In creative, empty it first.

blocks.text: Chests cannot be set down, opened or taken up on a server yet. Blasts, tracks, brushes, copy and blueprints leave chest cells alone.

In creative mode, press B to move to the next brush. The order is Block, Line, Wall, Floor, Replace, Copy, Blueprint, Bench, Railing and Roof. You can also pick a brush from the E > Build tab. {{creative-brush-cycle}}

items: Block: Right-click to place one block.
Line: Right-click once to set the first corner, aim at the far end and right-click again. The line follows the longer direction. {{brush-line-wall-floor}}
Wall: Same two clicks. The wall stands upright along the longer horizontal direction.
Floor: Same two clicks. The floor stays level at the height of the first corner.
Replace: Aim at a block of the material to swap and right-click. Aim at the opposite corner and right-click again. Matching blocks in the box become the block in your hand. {{brush-replace}}

Copy: Right-click two opposite corners to copy every block in that box except air and the Camp crate. Water and plants are copied too. Right-click again to paste at the ghost. R turns the paste 90 degrees. B discards the copy. {{brush-copy-paste}}
Blueprint: Save a build, then place it again. See the Blueprints section. {{creative-blueprints}}
Bench, Railing, Roof: One right-click stamps a fixed shape at the ghost. Press R first to turn it 90 degrees. {{brush-bench-railing-roof}}

blocks.text: Every brush except Block shows a ghost first. One action changes at most 512 half-metre pieces (64 whole blocks). Blueprints have their own limits. If a cell holds a solid block, nothing is built. Water and plants do not block a build. Replace is the exception: it swaps only the material you aim at. Hold Shift on the first click for half-metre steps.
Pressing B clears a corner selection or a copied selection. Copies are lost when you change brush or leave the world.
A blueprint is a build you save and place again. In creative mode it is free to place. In survival, placing it uses pieces from your pack. Blueprints do not work on servers yet.
Save a blueprint (creative)

items: Press [[B]] until the brush says **Blueprint**. You can also pick it in **E > Build**.
Aim at a ground corner of the build and press [[Shift]] + right-click. The status says **First corner set**.

Aim at the opposite ground corner and press [[Shift]] + right-click again. The **Structures** panel opens with a picture of what was taken. Nothing is saved yet. Until then, each corner you marked shows a post, and the box that would be saved is outlined. To cancel, press [[Shift]] + right-click on the same corner again.
Type a name and press **Save**. A name that is taken needs a second press to replace it. **Keep both** saves a copy called Name 2. Closing the panel discards the capture.
If you just placed a saved blueprint, its name is filled in and the panel says **Enter updates it**. Press **Enter**, then **Enter** again, to replace that file. Type another name to keep both.
Aim where you want it. The ghost shows the result. Right-click to build it. The whole build is one undo step, so [[Ctrl]]+[[Z]] removes it.

blocks.text: Build a blueprint in survival

items: Press [[B]] to take the Blueprint tool out. Press [[B]] again to put it away. In survival it is the only build tool, so [[B]] is the only key you need.
Aim where you want the build. The ghost turns red when you lack pieces.
Check the list on screen. It shows each material as carried / needed.
Right-click to build. The build is paid for in one go, or refused whole.

blocks.text: Each half-metre piece you change costs one piece of the item that block drops when mined. A whole block is 8 pieces. Dirt-type turf costs dirt. Voxels that already hold the right block cost nothing. If you lack any material, nothing is built or spent, and the status names the missing items.

rows: Lift the ghost 1 m up or down.
Delete the selected blueprint and its file.

blocks.text: The save leaves out water, cells you carved out of the terrain and the Camp crate. The status line says how many. A blueprint can be up to 128 m along any side and you can keep up to 64. Placement is refused if it would build over blocks you placed yourself or the Camp crate, or on top of you. Step back and try again.

Saved blueprints are plain files with the `.blueprint` extension in a folder named `blueprints`. The game looks for that folder where it starts. Without it, blueprints last only until you leave the session.

Sharing or importing blueprints and a survival materials list are not in this version. Saving a blueprint in survival is not checked in play yet. They are tracked in the {{structure-workshop-blueprints|feature ledger}}.
Press [[O]] to open the library. Each saved structure has its own picture. The picked one is shown large, with its size and piece count.

rows: Pick the previous or next structure.
Delete the picked structure. Press it twice to confirm.

blocks.text: Rename writes the new file before the old one is removed, so a failed rename keeps the original. The library holds up to 64 structures and does not search yet.
Checked at Voxelgame 9f915bcb. Not yet play-tested for this guide.

rows: The same actions, in the E > Build tab.

blocks.text: Undo covers brush actions, single blocks placed and blocks or trees you mined in creative. {{build-undo-redo}}

Undo is refused with "Undo blocked" if the cells changed since, if it would put a block inside you, or if it would pass the save's edit limit. Survival actions and explosions are not recorded. History is cleared when you leave the world.

The E > Build tab holds a searchable catalog of every item, the brush button, Undo and Redo, four preset palettes and a Save palette button. The Build tab is only offered in creative. {{creative-catalog}} {{build-workspace-palettes}}

items: Click an item to take one. Shift-click to take as many as fit in your pack.
Right-click an item to remove one you carry. Shift-right-click removes all of them.
Middle-click an item to star it.
Hover an item and press 1 to 0, or drag it onto a slot, to bind it to the hotbar.
Click Timber, Masonry, Coastal or Garden to fill the ten quick slots with that set. Slot 1 is selected.
Click Save palette to store your current ten slots.
Shift-click Save palette to load them back.

blocks.text: A preset replaces all ten quick slots. Click Save palette first if you want to keep them.

guides.title: Sailing a boat
guides.headline:
Launch it, steer it,
read the wind.
guides.summary: Launch and pack up the Small sailing boat, take the helm, set the sails, tack upwind and save your boats.
guides.lead: The Small sailing boat floats on any water in the game. You launch it from the hotbar, steer it from the helm and set the sails to catch the wind. Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet.

verification.method: Launch, pack, helm keys, sail and steering behaviour, wind speeds and saving come from the feature ledger, which cites the game source lines for each entry. The 6 m launch and pack range, 9 m helm range, 18 capacity of free pack room, 8-boat limit and 45 degree no-push zone are code values.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide and without screenshots. Test the tacking advice and the 45 degree no-push zone on open water before you rely on them.

blocks.text: Crafting the Small sailing boat selects it, ready to launch. Launching it works in creative and survival, and the boat can float on any water: sea, lakes and all six water types, at their real surface height. {{sailing-launch-and-pack}}

items: Select the Small sailing boat in your hotbar or inventory.
Look at open water within 6 m and right-click. The boat appears on the water.
In survival, the launch uses one boat item. In creative, the boat comes from the catalog and no item is used.

blocks.text: The launch needs water under the whole hull and clear room for the mast. If it fails, the game says "Boat needs clear water and room for its hull and mast (8 boats maximum)" and nothing is used. You can have up to 8 boats in the world at once.
Packing a boat puts it back into your pack, so you can carry it to another lake or sea. {{sailing-launch-and-pack}}

items: Walk up to a boat that has nobody at the helm and look at it from within 6 m.
Hold Shift and right-click. You can hold any item.
The boat goes into your pack. In survival, the boat item comes back to you.
You need 18 capacity of free pack room. A boat that is too heavy for your pack cannot be packed.
A boat with 0 health (wrecked) cannot be boarded or packed. The game clears it the next time you launch a boat.

blocks.text: Boats are not available on multiplayer servers yet. The game refuses with "Boats aren't available on servers yet".
You can walk and jump on the wooden deck like normal ground. The helm is where you steer and set the sails. {{sailing-helm-controls}}

rows: Take the helm, or step back to the cockpit. You must be within 9 m of the boat or on its deck.
Raise the sails. They follow over about 2 seconds.
Steer left or right. The rudder eases in and recentres.
Switch between first-person and chase view.
Look around freely without turning the boat.

items: There is no reverse. Lower the sails to slow down, and steer to turn.
The boat can turn while it is stopped.

The boat stops dead if its hull would run aground or hit another boat. It can only turn where the new heading still has water under the whole hull. If the boat is stuck on the shore, pack it up and launch it again.
Stepping off the helm stops the boat at once. Opening your pack with E pauses it.

blocks.text: Each world has one wind direction, and it never changes. The wind strength depends on the weather: about 2.8 m/s in clear weather and up to 8.5 m/s in a thunderstorm. Seasons do not change the wind. {{sailing-wind-and-tacking}}

items: Running with the wind (sailing straight downwind) is fastest.
Sailing across the wind gives about two-thirds of the wind speed.
Within 45 degrees of sailing straight into the wind, the sails give no push. To go upwind, zig-zag: sail one side of the wind, then turn across it to the other side. This is called tacking.

blocks.text: Read the flags

items: The red pennant at the top of the mast points downwind, the way the air travels.
The HUD flag shows the wind with the bow of your boat at the top of the screen.

blocks.text: The HUD bearing reads "TO n DEG", but it is not a compass bearing. 0 degrees points to +Z, which is south on the map, and 90 degrees points to +X, which is east. Use the flags to judge the wind.
Up to 8 launched boats are saved with their position, heading and health. Your boats are still there when you load the world. {{sailing-saving}}
If you save while at the helm, you reload standing in the stopped boat's cockpit, not at the helm. Press V to take the helm again.

guides.title: Settings and performance
guides.headline:
Settings,
and how to make the game run smoothly.
guides.summary: Where the settings are, what each General, Audio and Debug row does, and which ones to lower on a slower computer.
guides.lead: Open Settings with Esc in a world, or from the start menu. Settings are saved inside each world, so a new world copies the settings you have now.

verification.method: Each row, its default and its range come from the game source at the audited commit, b261ea8. The performance advice follows the notes on each row, including one offscreen GPU test on an Intel Iris Xe.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested, and no screenshots exist yet. The GPU numbers are from one test machine and will differ on yours.

items: In a world, press [[Esc]] to pause. Click **Settings**.
On the start menu, click **Settings**. Click **Back** to return.
Move between the **General**, **Audio**, **World** and **Debug** tabs with the mouse or [[Tab]] and [[Shift]] + [[Tab]].

rows: Click a chip or drag a slider
Step that value back. This is not shown in the game.

blocks.text: Hover a row label for a short description. The world stops advancing while Settings is open. {{settings-menu}}

items: **Shader**: None, Fast (default) or Cinematic. None is plain lighting for weak graphics cards. Fast adds sun shadows, sun rays and haze. Cinematic refines the shadows and rays and adds reflective water, at a higher frame-time cost. {{shader-tiers}}

**Horizon distance**: 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 (default), 96, 128, 192, 256 or 512 chunks. A chunk is 16 m, so 64 chunks reach about 1 km and 512 chunks reach about 8 km. Blocks close to you stay at full detail either way. {{horizon-distance}}
**Frame limit**: 60 (default), 120, 240 or Unlimited. The game does not use vsync, so this limit sets the pace. Study Grove always runs at about 30 FPS. {{frame-limit}}
**Atmospheric fog**: Light, Balanced (default) or Dense. Dense hides far terrain. The haze gets stronger with a longer horizon. Weather fog is separate. {{atmospheric-fog}}
**Field of view**: 60 to 96 degrees, in steps of 2 (default 72). A wider view shows more without changing how fast you move. {{field-of-view}}

**GUI size**: Auto (default), Small, Normal or Large. Auto uses 1.25x up to 1280x720 and 1.5x from 1920x1080 up. Small is 1.0x, Normal 1.25x and Large 1.75x. A small window caps the size so the UI still fits at least 800x450. {{gui-size}}
**Chunk fade-in**: on by default. New terrain fades in over 0.6 seconds. Turn it off to make terrain appear at once. Terrain prepared on the loading screen is always fully visible. {{chunk-fade-in}}
**Master volume**: 0% (mute) to 100% (default). It sets music, sound effects and nature sounds together, and applies at once. There is no separate volume for effects or ambience. {{master-volume}}
**Music**: turn the music on or off. Sound effects keep playing either way.
**Music speed**: 0.5x to 2.0x in steps of 0.1x. Tempo and pitch change together.
**Previous** and **Next** choose a song. The playlist then moves on by itself and loops. If no songs are found, the tab says so. {{music-player}}

blocks.text: Wind, rain, storms, forest, caves, birds, night wildlife, ponds and streams fade in and out around you without a setting. The ambience goes quiet in menus and underwater. {{nature-ambience}}

Most of the Debug tab is for checking the game, but two rows are useful for play. The **FPS and coordinates** box shows your frame rate with its limit, your X, Y and Z in metres and your biome. It is on by default, and it is back on after every load. {{fps-coordinates-readout}}

rows: Show or hide the performance overlay. It shows the frame time against your frame budget, the worst recent frame and the CPU work for the last half second.
Show or hide chunk borders. The chunk you stand in is gold.
Cycle the LOD view: Off, Tint and Colors. Cyan is full detail, and the other colours mark the distant stages.
Turn all three diagnostics off, or all on in Tint.

blocks.text: F7, F8 and F9 are reset to off when a world loads. F3 resets too. The Debug tab has the same switches. {{diagnostic-overlays}} {{performance-overlay}}

items: **Voxel view**: Off (default), Edges, which tints every block border, or X-ray, which draws only the outlines. {{voxel-view}}

**Distant terrain**: on by default. It draws the low-detail horizon beyond the nearby chunks. Turning it off saves work on slow machines. The view then ends at the loaded terrain, and new chunks can appear at that edge when you travel fast. {{distant-terrain-toggle}}
Set **Shader** to None.
Lower **Horizon distance** to 32 or 16 chunks.
Turn **Distant terrain** off on the Debug tab. The view then ends at the loaded terrain.
Press [[F3]] to see whether the frame time is above your frame budget. Red marks work that uses more than one CPU core or over half the frame budget.

blocks.text: Large horizons cost the most. One offscreen test on an Intel Iris Xe measured about 1.8 to 1.9 GiB of distant-terrain vertex buffers and about 37 to 39 ms of world GPU work at 256 to 512 chunks. Your numbers will differ. The overlay does not show GPU timing in normal play.
Graphics, audio and GUI settings are saved inside each world file. Create world copies the settings you have now. Loading another world switches to that world's own settings. {{per-world-settings}}
Planned: a 1024-chunk horizon. The largest option today is 512 chunks.
Planned: live GPU timings in the F3 overlay. Today the GPU box says it is unavailable in normal play.
Not in the game: the game does not keep the screen awake. Your system's power settings apply, including during long Study Grove sessions.
Planned: album art beside the song title, and a credits-only piece of music.

guides.title: Study Grove focus timer
guides.headline:
Study Grove,
a focus timer inside the game.
guides.summary: How to open Study Grove, run focus and break phases, change the lengths and choose a backdrop.
guides.lead: Study Grove is a countdown timer over a voxel landscape. It starts with 25 minutes of focus and 5 minutes of break, and it pauses the game while it is open.

verification.method: Each button label, default, range and key comes from the game source at the audited commit, e19e688: the timer logic in pomodoro.rs, the key handling in game.rs and the button labels in the render code. The start-menu entry and the P key are checked in the same commit.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested, and no screenshots exist yet. Chime and music timing depend on your audio setup.

items: In a world, press [[P]].
On the start menu, click **Study timer**.
Press [[P]] while you type in a search or name box and nothing opens. On the Worlds page, [[P]] also does nothing, so you can type a world name.

blocks.text: The world stops while Study Grove is open. In survival your needs and the world clock are paused too. Close it with [[Esc]] or **Back**. {{study-grove}}
The timer starts paused. Press [[Space]] or click **Start / resume** to run it, and **Pause** to stop it.

rows: Move to the next or previous button.
Leave Study Grove. The timer pauses.

items: **Reset phase** starts the current phase again from the beginning.
**To break** and **To study** switch phase at once. A switch does not count as a finished focus session.
The count of finished focus sessions is shown while Study Grove is open. It only goes up when a focus phase runs to the end.
A chime plays when a phase changes. Near the end of a break you hear a reminder 30 seconds before it ends. {{study-grove}}
**Focus** has - and + buttons. It goes from 5 to 90 minutes in steps of 5. The default is 25.
**Break** has - and + buttons. It goes from 1 to 30 minutes in steps of 1. The default is 5.

blocks.text: While the timer is paused, a change to a length applies at once. While it runs, the new length applies when the next phase starts.

items: **Chimes** turns the phase chimes and the break reminder on or off. On by default.
**Music** plays the music playlist while Study Grove is open, even when Music is off in Settings. Your Settings choice comes back when you leave. On by default.
**Auto-next** starts the next phase by itself when one ends. Turn it off to stop at the end of each phase. On by default.
**Animation** moves the scenery. Turn it off to hold the scene still. On by default.
**Weather** changes the look of the landscape: Clear, Rain, Snow or Sunset. It does not change your world's weather.

blocks.text: Planned: a small album-art picture beside the song title. Today the song title shows in Study Grove only as text. {{now-playing-album-art}}
Click **Backdrop** to switch from the landscape to **Backdrop: Real terrain**. The timer then sits over your actual world, so you can study with your builds in view. {{study-grove-real-terrain}}

items: **Camera: Your view** keeps the viewpoint you had.
**Camera: Slow orbit** turns slowly about 12 m around that point, above the treetops. Turn Animation off to hold it still.
**Weather** cycles through World, Clear, Rain, Mist and Sunset. The world's saved weather does not change.
**Options** shows every timer control over the compact timer. In the compact view, the other controls stay hidden until you click Options.

blocks.text: Your player, needs and clock stay paused. Leaving Study Grove puts your normal view back. Switching the backdrop resets the weather choice and closes Options.

items: Study Grove always runs at about 30 frames per second, whatever the frame limit is set to. {{frame-limit}}
The settings and the finished-session count reset when you restart the game or change world.

blocks.text: Planned: keeping the screen awake during long sessions. Today your system's power settings decide when the screen dims. {{display-awake}}

guides.title: Explosives: TNT and dynamite
guides.headline:
Blow up blocks
with TNT and dynamite.
guides.summary: Place and light TNT with G, read the blast reach, throw dynamite, and see which explosives survival can craft.
guides.lead: TNT and dynamite break blocks in a wide circle. Blasted blocks are destroyed, not collected. Creative players can use them freely. In survival, both need Glow crystal, which the world does not generate naturally.

verification.method: Controls, fuse times, blast reach, damage rules and dynamite throwing come from the game source at the ledger's audited commit dd29d91 (game.rs, explosives.rs, projectile.rs, ranged_input.rs, inventory.rs). Blast distances are calculated from code constants, not measured in play.
verification.limits: Source-checked, not play-tested in this guide. No explosion screenshots exist yet, so the blast sizes are not checked against a headless capture.

items: Select TNT in your hotbar.
Right click a surface to place a whole block. Hold Shift and right click to place one half-metre charge.
Aim at the TNT, within 6 m, and press [[G]].
Step back. The fuse lasts 2.6 seconds.

rows: Light the aimed TNT and every TNT piece touching it, even diagonally.
Mine TNT back without lighting it.

blocks.text: Lit TNT pops loose and can fall, roll or float before it blows. Touching pieces go off together as one blast. {{tnt-place-and-ignite}}
G does not work on multiplayer servers. The game shows "Explosives aren't available on servers yet".

items: One half-metre charge or one dynamite stick: about 1.5 m.
One whole TNT block: about 4.25 m.
A touching group of TNT: up to about 10.5 m, which needs about 62 touching TNT blocks.

blocks.text: A whole TNT block cannot break obsidian. Solid stone only gives way close to the charge. Blocks between the charge and a target absorb part of the blast, and water absorbs a lot of it. {{explosion-effects}}
Explosions cannot be undone. Blasted blocks are gone. The status line counts cleared half-metre voxels.
In survival, players near a blast lose health and are knocked back. Creative players take no damage. Creatures are hurt in both modes.
Stand well back before you light a group. The blast reaches about 10.5 m from the largest group.

items: Select Dynamite in your hotbar.
Hold right click to wind up. A longer wind-up throws farther.
Release to throw. The fuse starts on release.
Take cover. The stick goes off 2.3 seconds after you throw it, where it is then. It sticks to the first surface it hits.

rows: Wind up and throw a dynamite stick.

items: The stick sticks to the first surface it hits, including walls and ceilings.
You cannot place blocks while you hold dynamite.
Opening a menu cancels a wind-up.
